title: First archaeological identification of nixtamalized maize, from two pit latrines at the ancient Maya site of San Bartolo, Guatemala
version: Journal of Archaeological Science 143, 105581, DOI 10.1016/j.jas.2022.105581; author-shared article rendered as HTML text
lineage: Original excavated assemblage and laboratory analysis. Article sections and figure captions were read in the author-shared article rendering. PDF bytes and supplementary materials were unavailable. The analytical comparison uses Johnson and Marston’s earlier experiment and shares one author.

passages.note: Grupo Zacatal pits and the contextual, most likely use interval of c. 770–895 cal CE. The underlying calibrated charcoal intervals are discontiguous.

Microscopic and elemental comparison with experimental nixtamalized maize. The authors discuss distinguishing starch spherulites from fecal formations and their reasons for discounting alteration after burial.
The authors interpret the deposits as likely including cooking wastewater and human waste.
